- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., +0.27 or +0.32) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., -0.11 or 0.00) — model fails to recognize downward pressure.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then overcorrects in the opposite direction.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in early periods — model often misses immediate downward corrections after sentiment shifts.
- When sentiment is positive and price is rising, model tends to project higher continuation, but true outcome often shows a pullback within 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, model often underestimates the magnitude of the next drop — especially in the first 10 days of forecast.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends when sentiment is mixed — model overfits to recent highs/lows without accounting for sentiment reversal signals.
